title: Savings & Money Market Accounts: The Comparison Balance in a Money Market Upgrade
content:
Choosing the highest money market tier an owner qualifies for means setting a Savings & Money Market Accounts product's funds against each tier's minimum. This page defines the figure that is set against those minimums, here called the Comparison Balance, and the state the account's ledger must be in for that figure to be read.

## Definition of the Comparison Balance

The Comparison Balance is the account's present posted Balance in its corrected form:

- it includes every refund the account is owed, credited to the account; a Balance that is missing an owed refund is not the Comparison Balance;
- where the owner moves money out of the account during the same contact, it is the Balance with that transfer taken out.

## State of the ledger

A target is picked only while no entry on the account bears a posting date lying after the current date, as the ledger itself shows. That is what guarantees the posted Balance reflects every transfer and refund it ought to.

Entries made on a weekend day or on one of the Federal Reserve's holidays are posted on the following business day. So long as any entry is dated after the current date, the policy picks no target. The ledger shows whether this holds, and the target itself does not test it; it is a precondition for applying the policy.

## Points of judgement

**The ledger shows a refund dated next Monday. Can a target be picked today?** No. An entry dated after the current date means the policy is not applied.
